s01.t29: A complete system to generate high-quality leads on LinkedIn without cold pitching. Audience clarity, content authority, personal outreach, nurturing, and consistent follow-up, combined into one repeatable framework.

s02.t01: From Tejas Jhaveri, founder to founder
s02.t02: Tejas isn't your average marketer. He's a 4x entrepreneur who built Flintstop, a D2C eCommerce brand, into a $6M-a-year machine, shipping out 8,000 orders a day before selling the business in 2020. At Myntmore, his B2B outbound agency, he's helped 130+ B2B companies book 12K+ meetings and generate $120M+ in pipeline. He's a TEDx speaker, angel investor, and has taught B2B growth methodologies at IIT and IIM. Now, he's here to do it for you.
s02.t03: Most people treat LinkedIn lead generation as either constant posting or cold pitching. Neither works on its own. This framework combines five moving parts, audience, content, outreach, nurture, and follow-up, into one system, so leads show up consistently without you sounding like a sales bot in anyone's inbox.

s03.t02: Why this matters: the more precise your audience, the higher the quality of leads and the easier it is to write messages that land.
s03.t03: Job role, company size, industry, location
s03.t05: LinkedIn activity, content engagement, decision-making authority
s03.t06: Identify the top 20% of leads most likely to engage, map 2–3 key pain points per ICP, and document it all: ICP name, role, pain point, decision criteria, preferred content type. Two examples to start from:
s03.t07: Keep updating your ICPs as you learn from real responses and engagement, they're a working document, not a one-time exercise.

s04.t02: Why this matters: people reach out to those they already trust and see as experts, before any business conversation starts.
s04.t03: Plan content that answers your audience's most common questions, using posts, carousels, videos, polls, and newsletters. Include storytelling, real wins, real failures, real lessons, and make sure it actually demonstrates experience and expertise, not just claims it.
s04.t04: Post a carousel on "3 Steps to Boost LinkedIn Lead Gen Without Ads," share a short video walking through a recent client result, or run a poll asking your ICP directly what their biggest challenge is right now. Then repurpose all of it into your outreach and nurture messages later.

s05.t02: Why this matters: thoughtful outreach builds a connection without ever feeling like a sales pitch.
s05.t03: Send a personalized connection request referencing their profile, recent activity, or a company milestone, then follow up with a sequence of three thoughtful messages: appreciation, value, then a soft, low-pressure invitation.

s06.t02: Why this matters: leads rarely convert on the first touch, staying visible is what increases the odds of a real conversation.
s06.t03: Engage consistently with your leads' content, like, comment, and add real insight. Share valuable posts and industry trends periodically, and track each lead's interactions so you know their interest level and what the right next action is.

s07.t02: Why this matters: consistent, respectful follow-up is what converts a lead without ever being pushy about it.
s07.t03: Follow up 3–7 days after the initial outreach if there's no response, adding a new insight or resource each time rather than repeating yourself. Adjust the tone based on prior engagement, and mix up the touchpoint: a DM, a comment on their post, or a piece of content shared directly.

s08.t02: If you're looking to optimize your LinkedIn profile and turn it into a growth engine, you're in the right place. Whether you're a founder, CXO, or consultant, LinkedIn can become your #1 inbound channel.
